appraisal_events.evidence: chaque duchesse allait droit au baron, comme si c'était lui qui avait reçu, et disait, juste à un pas des Verdurin, qui entendaient tout : « Montrez-moi où est la mère Verdurin... elle n'a pas trop mauvaise façon. »... M. de Charlus... oublia entièrement Mme Verdurin et la laissa oublier, jusqu'au scandale, par les gens « de son monde ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus's aristocratic guests treat the salon as his alone, mocking Mme Verdurin as 'la mère Verdurin' within her own hearing and bypassing her as hostess, a rudeness the narrator says the negligent Charlus let go on to the point of scandal.

appraisal_events.evidence: la reine de Naples... se mit à causer avec Mme Verdurin comme si elle était venue pour le plaisir de la voir... fit mille déclarations à la Patronne, ne tarit pas sur l'envie qu'elle avait depuis si longtemps de faire sa connaissance, la complimenta sur sa maison... voyant Mme Verdurin seule et délaissée... avait cherché à feindre que... le centre de cette soirée... c'était Mme Verdurin.
appraisal_events.explanation: Seeing Mme Verdurin abandoned by the other guests, the queen deliberately singles her out with warm, generous attention and treats her as the true reason for her visit.

appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Charlus, redressant sa taille en arrière... prit une expression de prophète et regarda l'assemblée avec un sérieux qui signifiait que ce n'était pas le moment de rire, et dont on vit rougir brusquement le visage de plus d'une invitée prise en faute... le respect pour la musique — de par le prestige de Palamède — avait été subitement inculqué à une foule aussi mal élevée qu'élégante.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus reasserts commanding authority over his unruly guests, shaming them into reverent silence for the music, though the narrator frames his prophet-like posturing as comic even while granting its real effect.

status_effects.explanation: The guests bypass her entirely as hostess, addressing only Charlus and discussing her dismissively within earshot instead of greeting her as mistress of the house.
The duchesses' condescending remarks about her appearance and name ('elle n'a pas trop mauvaise façon') mock her in front of others who overhear.
The narrator opens by stating plainly that this evening's negligence toward Mme Verdurin was what began Charlus's ruin, since he let his own guests scandalously ignore her.
The queen showers her with compliments and declares a longstanding wish to know her, a direct and generous personal esteem.
Seeing her abandoned by the crowd, the queen visibly and deliberately treats her as the evening's true center, a witnessed act of royal favor that restores her standing before the room.
His stern authority visibly cows a fashionable but ill-mannered crowd into silence and respect, a real if somewhat ridiculous display of command.

ambiguities: The narrator's account of Charlus once sharply criticizing Mme de Vaugoubert for a similar social misstep (failing to redirect royal favor toward others) is recalled here as dramatic irony, since Charlus is shown repeating that very error toward Mme Verdurin in E1; this parallel is context for his diminishment rather than an independent event.
